You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
node.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Examine vegetation, hills, sky, foreground ground and the left-side structure separately. Identify contours, layered marks or rubbed shading that construct each region's depicted forms or planes, then assess whether substantial environmental areas have been re-expressed. Smooth or simplified passages are allowed: discrete strokes are not required everywhere. Distinguish blended chalk passages that define forms through boundaries, layering or pigment variation from undifferentiated tonal smears. Grain, diagonal streaking and reduced photographic detail alone do not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas retain photographic modeling with only blur or texture, even if some vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Retained composition is not evidence of failure. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect vegetation, distant hills, sky, foreground ground and the left-side structure independently of the giraffes. Give region-specific evidence of what constructs the depicted forms: drawn boundaries, layered marks, form-following rubbed shading, or retained photographic modeling under blur or texture. Evaluate substantial environmental coverage without allowing one locally drawn region to stand in for the rest.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image adds chalk-like grain and broad diagonal smearing, but most environmental regions are not clearly constructed as drawn forms. Vegetation is reduced to soft green masses with little distinct layered mark-making; the hills and sky are largely blended gray-blue tonal areas; and the foreground ground is a smooth, streaked wash rather than chalk shading that defines its planes. The left-side structure retains its photographic-looking rails and posts with softened edges. Thus substantial scenery appears blurred or textured rather than re-expressed as a chalk drawing.
